title: Longest Common Prefix: vertical scan comparing characters.
shortTitle: Longest Common Prefix: Vertical Scan Comparing Characters
keyPoints: Vertical scan treats strings as rows of a grid and checks each column position across all strings.
Use the first string as a reference and compare its character at each position against the same position in every other string.
Stop at the first position where any string has ended or shows a different character.
Time complexity is O(S) where S is the sum of all characters examined, with early termination when the prefix is short.
Handle edge cases: empty array returns empty string, any empty string means the common prefix is empty.
Alternative approaches include horizontal scan, binary search on prefix length, divide and conquer, and trie.

s1_definition.oneliner: Scan character positions top to bottom across all strings and stop at the first mismatch or end.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Vertical scan** treats the string array like a grid with each string as a row, scanning column by column.
- **Reference string** is the first string in the array, and each of its character positions is compared against the same position in every other string.
- **Early termination** stops the scan the moment any string is shorter than the current position or shows a different character.
- **Time complexity** is O(S) where S is the total characters examined, which is at most the number of strings times the prefix length.
- **Edge cases** include an empty array (returns empty string) and any empty string (prefix is immediately empty).
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India has a batch of account numbers that share a common branch prefix. A clerk wants the longest leading portion identical across all of them. The clerk reads the first character of every number: if they all match, keep it and move to the second character. The moment one number runs out of digits or shows a different character, the shared prefix ends right there.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Strings:  "HDFC001"  "HDFC012"  "HDFC002"

  Column 0:  H  H  H  ── all match
  Column 1:  D  D  D  ── all match
  Column 2:  F  F  F  ── all match
  Column 3:  C  C  C  ── all match
  Column 4:  0  0  0  ── all match
  Column 5:  0  1  0  ── MISMATCH at string[1]
                          │
                          ▼
                   return "HDFC0"

  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Vertical Scan Algorithm          │
  │                                   │
  │  for each column i:               │
  │    c = first[i]                   │
  │    for each string s:             │
  │      if i >= s.length ── STOP     │
  │      if s[i] != c    ── STOP      │
  │    all match ── continue          │
  │                                   │
  │  return first (all matched)       │
  └──────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The Longest Common Prefix problem finds the longest starting substring shared by every string in an array, and vertical scan is the cleanest approach for it. Rajesh at the National Bank of India uses this to identify the common branch prefix in a batch of account numbers. The algorithm treats the strings like rows of a grid and scans down each column, comparing the character at each position across all strings and stopping at the first mismatch or at the end of any string.

The efficiency comes from early termination. When the shared prefix is short, which is typical for account numbers that differ after the branch code, the scan examines very few characters even if the strings are long. The worst case, where all strings are identical, examines every character exactly once per string, which is the total input size and is unavoidable.

Edge cases matter: an empty array returns an empty string, a single string is its own prefix, and any empty string in the array means the prefix is immediately empty. The most common bug is not checking whether a string is shorter than the current column index before accessing its character, which causes a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.

Vertical scan has the best early-exit behavior among the common approaches. Horizontal scan folds the prefix pairwise but is less direct. Binary search on the prefix length adds a log factor. A trie gives O(S) time but uses O(S) extra space and is worth it only when you need to query the prefix of different subsets repeatedly.

Remember one sentence: scan each column across all strings, stop at the first mismatch or end, and return the reference substring up to that point.
